title: Control of working memory by phase–amplitude coupling of human hippocampal neurons
goal: Reproduce the source-defined load-dependent LFP PAC finding, beginning with the complete Figure 2d author-selected example and the registered single-unit PAC model comparisons, preserving source trial eligibility, spike/LFP alignment, transformations and necessary model/null controls. Report any eligible-patient extension separately. Evaluate improvement of that same PAC finding only when a scientifically justified, source-compatible criterion is established. Keep five-category decoding as a distinct secondary empirical result; it cannot satisfy the primary PAC reproduction or improvement claim.
primary_outputs: Reproduction: executable analysis and source-native outputs for the corrected primary empirical findings: The retained empirical Figure 2d load-1/load-3 LFP phase-amplitude curves and Tort comodulograms plus registered single-unit PAC model comparisons, beginning with source-defined examples and indispensable controls. No automatic whole-paper, complete-population or every-figure claim; the declared eligible-patient extension is reported separately.
Primary improvement: unavailable until a source-grounded same-result comparison is independently justified; no new score or direction is implied.

Retained secondary work: Preserve Figure 6 maintenance/session-ensemble five-category decoding and Extended Data Figure 7a encoding pseudo-population decoding as distinct secondary empirical alternatives, not interchangeable baselines or primary PAC outcomes. Extended Data Figure 6 simulations explain necessary PAC-selection controls; the released Figure 6f binary-geometry simulation is partial methodological support and does not establish the empirical decoder or PAC finding. Retain eligible-patient extension work as separately declared prospective scope, not exact-example reproduction. Selecting a decoder as replacement primary would require a new scientific scope decision.
